title: Replay an immediately disputed turn under a new campaign rule
description:
Objective
Handle a player objection to the current/immediately preceding adjudication by establishing an approved ruling or house rule effective from the start of that disputed turn, restoring pre-turn state, and replaying once under the new rule.

Required behavior
Recognize an explicit objection to the immediate adjudication, obtain player-approved prose/kind, persist canonical rule identity with effective position at disputed-turn start, restore the checkpoint/state immediately before that turn, replay the same player turn with the rule active in both DM and auditor contexts, and commit the accepted replay as campaign canon. Required canonical-conflict scenario: after a material-component rejection, "we don't use spell components" creates a house rule, rolls back the disputed turn, replays under it, and commits the replay. Abandoned adjudication may remain diagnostic/provenance history but not continuing campaign canon.

Architecture and references
Use eshyra-jhpt.1-.4 for domain/storage/context parity, audited-turn staging eshyra-67qo, turn rollback proof eshyra-c07.8, and checkpoint restore foundation eshyra-7wc.5. Preserve canonical campaign history and auditor evidence across the replay boundary.

Non-goals
No arbitrary historical retroactivity or replay of older turns; no automatic objection inference; no rule without player approval; no prose-to-mechanics compiler; no automatic house rule from an unaccepted canonical violation; no changes to immutable pack semantics.
acceptance_criteria: An immediate material-components objection creates approved house-rule prose effective at disputed-turn start, restores exact pre-turn state, replays once with identical DM/auditor active rules, and makes accepted replay canonical; ordinary new rules remain prospective; failed replay preserves a recoverable canonical pre-turn state; older-turn retroactivity is rejected; diagnostic history distinguishes abandoned and canonical attempts.
